title: Spherical harmonics light probe from radiance
purpose: Project a radiance function or an equirectangular image onto nine RGB spherical harmonic coefficients with exact solid-angle weights, evaluate the diffuse irradiance they give, and build a three.js LightProbe from them. Use it for cheap ambient lighting from a procedural sky or an environment image without baking.

engine.name: webgl2_browser
engine.notes: The projection and evaluation need no three.js; toLightProbe takes three.js as THREE (SphericalHarmonics3, LightProbe); only 0.186.1 was run.

contract.coefficient_layout: Float64Array of 27: coefficient by coefficient (c0 r, c0 g, c0 b, c1 r, ...) in three.js SphericalHarmonics3 order 1, y, z, x, xy, yz, 3z^2 - 1, xz, x^2 - y^2; radiance projections, not pre-convolved

limits: Nine coefficients hold only low-frequency light: sharp suns, shadows and occlusion are lost, and the band-limited result rings, so irradiance can dip slightly below zero opposite a strong light (about -0.016 for a top light). Diffuse only; it gives no specular reflections. The projection is a midpoint sum over a latitude-longitude grid with exact cell solid angles: a constant integrates exactly, other functions within about 1e-3 at the default 64 x 128 grid, and a light smaller than a grid cell is undersampled. Equirectangular rows must run from +Y to -Y. Only three.js 0.186.1 was run, in headless Chrome on SwiftShader WebGL 2.
technique_references: Real spherical harmonics of bands 0 to 2
Irradiance from the cosine-lobe convolution (Ramamoorthi and Hanrahan)
Latitude-longitude quadrature with exact solid angles
